text:
Omar Chen: thinking out loud — we should add a compact 'provenance' search in the Console: a single-line timeline per resource that shows actor, action, and a short diff hash. useful for quick triage without loading full ndjson exports.

Priya Nair: +1. is this separate from the existing change-timeline? want to keep perf fast for orgs with huge event volumes.

Benji Cole: idea: store a precomputed compact summary for each change event (actor, verb, target, small tokenized label) and surface via an index. then full export stays as ndjson. compact view = cheap queries and paginated.

Marta Vega: how does this interact with retention/PII? If compact summary still contains sensitive keys we need redaction or redaction flags.

Omar Chen: yep — two modes: compact-redacted (PII removed) and compact-full (for admins with export perms). compact-redacted used for most console views.

Priya Nair: telemetry ask: we need metrics for compact view cache hit rate, avg fetch latency, and how often users escalate from compact -> full export. helps optimize precompute TTL.

Benji Cole: also quota note: exports (full ndjson) are heavy. should count toward export quota separately from api read quota. otherwise customers hitting the button will blow through credits.

Marta Vega: UX: show a tiny preview line and an inline "download" button that requests a presigned url. Clicking opens a modal with scope & retention info and an indicator if export will be sampled.

Omar Chen: sample flow sketch: user requests export -> server checks perms -> if volume > threshold, return sampled export unless user checks "full export (admin only)" -> audit log event created for export action. We must surface that export action in compact view as its own provenance entry.

Priya Nair: security: export events need additional attribution (requesting user, approved-by if escalated, ip, region). also sign with export-id for later verifiable chain.

Benji Cole: rough API example for presign:
```
POST /v1/exports
{ "scope": "tenant:abc", "from": 1680000000, "to": 1740000000, "mode": "compact|full", "sample_rate": 0.01 }
Response: { "export_id": "exp_...", "status": "pending", "presign_url": null }
```
When ready, presign_url returned.

Marta Vega: question: should compact items be stored in the same eventstore or a separate real-time index (ES)? If we use ES we get fast UI search but more infra cost.

Omar Chen: prefer separate compact index (Elasticsearch or vector store) populated by a streaming job that consumes events post-write and writes summaries. Keeps primary eventstore immutable and cheaper.

Priya Nair: ops note: need backpressure and reindex endpoints for rebuilds. and a retention policy for compact index (maybe 90 days by default).

Benji Cole: export pricing UX: warn user if expected file size > 100MB and give an estimate. plus an opt-in email when ready.

Marta Vega: implementation TODOs: 1) schema for compact-summary (actor, verb, target, redaction_flags, change_hash, export_refs) 2) streaming job + index 3) console UI + modal 4) export API + quota enforcement 5) telemetry events & dashboards.

Omar Chen: I'm going to sketch schema and API changes this afternoon, will post a short PR for review. tagging @console-bot to create a tracking ticket.

console-bot: Created ticket PLAT-5287: "Compact provenance index + presigned export flow" assigned to Omar Chen. :white_check_mark:

Priya Nair: thanks — small follow-up: add an admin-only endpoint to retrieve raw export metadata (export_id, signer, checksum) for compliance teams.

Benji Cole: noted. I'll add export metadata to the ndjson envelope so downstream consumers can verify checksums.

Marta Vega: great. low-priority UX ask: add a heatmap at org-level showing export frequency by team so compliance can spot risky behavior.

Omar Chen: love that. we'll capture export events with team labels so the heatmap is trivial to build in Analytics.

Priya Nair: ok cool — will add telemetry dimensions in the ticket.

Benji Cole: merging design notes into the ticket now. short follow-ups in thread if anything else. :rocket:
